sources.text: Paragraph 11 asks the Secretary-General to continue regular country-specific reporting on the humanitarian situation and response, including famine and food-insecurity risk. Paragraph 12 separately requests swift reporting to the Council when the relevant risk arises in armed conflict.

Russia argued that food insecurity also reflects factors outside armed conflict, including natural disasters and unilateral economic restrictions. It said the broader food-security problem extended beyond the Security Council's scope.

comparison: Russia argued the Council's provision does not cover non-conflict food insecurity, while the clause mandates continued reporting on all humanitarian risks and swift reporting when conflict-related risks arise.
